      "conditions": ["A project adopts the profile for a named realisation boundary."],
      "definition": "DESIGN_MODULE is optional material family F17, software design. Actors enter it when designing, implementing or reviewing a governed boundary. Its foundation-to-law table distinguishes derived consequences from domain and policy choices and their owners.",
      "exceptions": [],
      "grounding": [{"end_line":174,"quote":"Its instance premises hold where a project\nadopts this profile for a boundary; they are adopted with it and do not\nfollow from the foundations (P1, P6):","section_id":"repo://stdo-v3-common/35fb4824a064a84df5af214a0d0e2da597c18ac6/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md#DESIGN_MODULE%2F1.%20Purpose%20and%20position%2FFoundation%20to%20law","start_line":172}],
      "key":"design_profile",
      "label":"Software design profile, F17"
    },
    {
      "conditions": [],
      "definition": "The table's cited commitments have distinct standing: P0 recovered; P1, P2, P3, P4a and P6 independent; P4b derived from P0 and P2 with P0's non-reacquirable step-fact premise; P5 derived from P0 and P6 with P0's open-world premise. Imported families are F1 frames/context, F2 transitions/steps/configuration, F3 results/combination, F4 work state/resumption/reuse, F6 claims/evidence/assessment/acceptance, F8 identity, F10 constitutional chain/outcome/build-tenant binding, F12 project adoption, F13 work carriers, and F18 graph-native construction. Adopted instance premises are I1 decided outcomes/capabilities and named-boundary adoption; I2 alternative and possibly multiple code locations for one meaning; I3 bounded actors whose later actions generally lack original design reasoning; I4 local or existing-foundation mechanisms and recurrence across boundaries and time.",
      "exceptions": [],
      "grounding": [{"end_line":187,"quote":"- I4: a mechanism the boundary needs can be built locally or taken from\n  existing foundations, and similar computation recurs across boundaries\n  and over time.","section_id":"repo://stdo-v3-common/35fb4824a064a84df5af214a0d0e2da597c18ac6/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md#DESIGN_MODULE%2F1.%20Purpose%20and%20position%2FFoundation%20to%20law","start_line":185}],
      "key":"foundation_premises",
      "label":"Commitments, imports and instance premises"
    },
    {

      "grounding": [{"end_line":231,"quote":"Consumers of these rows, where an actor enters them (FOUNDATIONS §3\nFoundation to law, Consumers), one list per row, each consumer linked to\nits own locus:","section_id":"repo://stdo-v3-common/35fb4824a064a84df5af214a0d0e2da597c18ac6/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md#DESIGN_MODULE%2F1.%20Purpose%20and%20position%2FFoundation%20to%20law","start_line":229}],
      "key":"referenced_rule_loci",
      "label":"Referenced owning and consuming rule loci"
    },
    {
      "conditions": ["The Product is governed by the graph-execution profile."],
      "definition": "For Product movement between typed asset states, the governing structure is outcome traversal, then declarative graph carriers (GTL and ABG), then deterministic module realisation. A module is a realisation cut inside this graph program, not the program itself.",
      "exceptions": [],
      "grounding": [{"end_line":280,"quote":"1. outcome traversal under the graph-execution profile;\n2. the declarative graph carrier structure (GTL and ABG in that profile's\n   terms); and\n3. deterministic module realisation under this profile.","section_id":"repo://stdo-v3-common/35fb4824a064a84df5af214a0d0e2da597c18ac6/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md#DESIGN_MODULE%2F2.%20Graph-execution%20alignment%20and%20escalation","start_line":277}],
      "key":"graph_realisation_alignment",
      "label":"Graph-execution and module alignment"
    },
    {
      "conditions": ["The profile governs the boundary."],
      "definition": "Three overriding boundary-closure evaluators are authority seam closure, essential carrier consolidation and enforcement after proof. Ingress collapse specifies the accompanying foreign-input boundary discipline.",
      "exceptions": [],
      "grounding": [{"end_line":304,"quote":"When this profile governs a boundary, each design or implementation change\nshould be judged against three overriding evaluators (P6, P2). A\nchange that improves local ergonomics, test output or static-checker\noutput but fails one of them is not real progress under this profile.","section_id":"repo://stdo-v3-common/35fb4824a064a84df5af214a0d0e2da597c18ac6/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md#DESIGN_MODULE%2F3.%20Boundary%20closure%20evaluators","start_line":301}],

    },
    {
      "conditions": ["B is one governed boundary."],
      "definition": "M(B) is the complete material-relation network: entities; identities; relationships; cardinalities; invariants; authorities; authority transitions; functions; higher-order composition laws; topology; lifecycle states and transitions; public contracts; externally observable Product meaning; declared domains and admission conditions; failure and refusal routes; effect and closure laws; projections; module mappings; material algorithmic obligations. U(B) is its unresolved subset. Decision completeness requires empty U(B), joint satisfiability, and semantic equivalence of every admitted network under governing Product, requirements and accepted design relations. Co-evolution admissibility is exactly decision completeness. The design gate is the smallest causally closed affected set needed to establish it.",
      "exceptions": [],
      "grounding": [{"end_line":502,"quote":"U(B) = unresolved(M(B))\ndecision_complete(B) iff\n  U(B) = empty\n  and M(B) is jointly satisfiable\n  and every network admitted by M(B) is semantically equivalent under the\n      governing Product, requirements and accepted design relations\nco_evolution_admissible(B) iff decision_complete(B)\ndesign_gate(B) =\n  the smallest causally closed affected set needed to establish\n  decision_complete(B)","section_id":"repo://stdo-v3-common/35fb4824a064a84df5af214a0d0e2da597c18ac6/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md#DESIGN_MODULE%2F5.%20Ontology-first%20design%2FProportional%20design%20sequencing","start_line":493},{"end_line":571,"quote":"M(B) =\n  entities + identities + relationships + cardinalities + invariants\n  + authorities + authority transitions + functions\n  + higher-order composition laws + topology\n  + lifecycle states and transitions + public contracts\n  + externally observable Product meaning\n  + declared domains and admission conditions\n  + failure and refusal routes + effect and closure laws\n  + projections + module mappings + material algorithmic obligations","section_id":"repo://stdo-v3-common/35fb4824a064a84df5af214a0d0e2da597c18ac6/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md#DESIGN_MODULE%2F5.%20Ontology-first%20design%2FDecision-complete%20symbolic%20design","start_line":563}],

      "grounding": [{"end_line":669,"quote":"This is a constructability obligation,\nnot a prescribed implementation; the consumer chooses the substrate and the\nevidence mechanism (P0).","section_id":"repo://stdo-v3-common/35fb4824a064a84df5af214a0d0e2da597c18ac6/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md#DESIGN_MODULE%2F5.%20Ontology-first%20design%2FNative%20constructability%20%28UP-002%29","start_line":667},{"end_line":680,"quote":"Native constructability proves that the selected substrate can realise the\ndesign; it does not prove that locally constructing another generic\nmechanism is the best realisation.","section_id":"repo://stdo-v3-common/35fb4824a064a84df5af214a0d0e2da597c18ac6/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md#DESIGN_MODULE%2F5.%20Ontology-first%20design%2FCapability%20and%20foundation%20selection%20%28UP-023%29","start_line":673}],
